title: How do we draw a perpendicular from a point outside a line?
description: An arc from the point cuts the line at two places, so the point is equally far from both. Arcs from those two places meet at a second point, and the line through the two points is the perpendicular bisector.
teaching_notes: One idea: a point equally far from two places on a line lies on their perpendicular bisector, so two such points give the perpendicular. Watch for students who change the compass opening between the two lower arcs.

video_script.why: The child uses equal arcs and the perpendicular bisector to draw a perpendicular from a point outside a line.
video_script.substitution: Equal arcs make a point equally far from the two ends of a segment on the line.
video_script.anchor: A line l with a point P marked outside it, an unmarked ruler and a compass.
video_script.payoff_line: The line P Q is perpendicular to l and passes through P.

final_answer.value: PQ is perpendicular to l and passes through P
final_answer.spoken: the line P Q is perpendicular to l and passes through P

hold_back: PQ is perpendicular to l and passes through P
maths_rules: Centre P, a large enough radius: an arc cuts l at X and Y, so PX = PY.
P is equally far from X and Y, so P lies on the perpendicular bisector of XY.
Centres X and Y, one radius, arcs on the other side of l meet at Q, so QX = QY and Q lies on the same bisector.
Join P and Q; PQ meets l at O. Two points fix the line, so PQ is the perpendicular bisector of XY.
Check: XO = OY with the ruler, and the angle at O is a right angle.
video_script.design: One line l, one outside point P. Two equal arcs make X and Y, then two equal arcs on the other side make Q. The method is the equal-arc method of the earlier video.
